SMTO-DB-0013 — SMTO can only search PostgreSQL servers for databases

GUID: 23a04a44-21cd-4390-bd42-9c2f94f78e1e
Slug: database-discovery-engine-unsupported
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to find the databases on a server of a type it can't search. This search only works with PostgreSQL servers. SMTO didn't connect to anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check what kind of database server it is. If it is PostgreSQL, set the engine (database type) in the request to postgres and send it again. SMTO only accepts the names postgres or postgresql here, so other spellings are refused.
  2. If the server is another type, such as MySQL or Oracle, ask the person who manages SMTO whether another Skill is set up for it. This search can't connect to other kinds of database servers, whatever settings you choose.

What success looks like

  • The search lists the databases found on the PostgreSQL server as drafts you can review.

If it still fails

  • Send the request you used to the person who manages SMTO, without the password, and say what kind of database server it is. Don't label a different kind of server as PostgreSQL to get past this check.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A database discovery request named a nonempty engine other than postgres/postgresql and was rejected as unsupported_engine before any connection was attempted.

What this means

  • Discovery accepts postgres/postgresql normalization but rejects a different nonempty engine as unsupported_engine. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • Discovery accepts postgres/postgresql normalization but rejects a different nonempty engine as unsupported_engine.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the normalized engine to this route's PostgreSQL support.

How to fix it

  • Discovery normalizes engine to postgresql only for postgres or postgresql; any other value (for example mysql) is rejected. Send engine=postgres for a PostgreSQL server; other engines need a separately supported Skill rather than this discovery flow.
  • Use engine postgres in this flow, or use a separate supported capability for the intended database engine.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported engine uses this route, or another capability handles the intended backend.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
